headerDisplay: Adds one or more virtual on/off lights. Every light triggers a configurable number of virtual single-press switches, one at a time in rotation, each time the light is turned on — whether from the Home app, Siri, or an automation. Point HomeKit automations at each switch's "Single Press" event to chain further actions.
footerDisplay: See the plugin README for a full walkthrough of the round-robin switch behavior and example automations.

name.title: Light Name
name.description: Displayed name of the virtual light. Must be unique across all lights in this plugin.

switchCount.title: Number of Switches
switchCount.description: How many virtual single-press switches accompany this light.

resetCountOnOff.title: Reset switch sequence when the light turns off
resetCountOnOff.description: Off (default): the rotation never resets — turning the light on repeatedly keeps cycling through the switches no matter how many times it's turned off in between. On: turning the light off resets the rotation, so the next time it's turned on, switch 1 fires again.

turnOffOnCycleComplete.title: Turn off the light when a cycle completes
turnOffOnCycleComplete.description: Off (default): the light stays on after firing a switch. On: as soon as the last switch in the rotation fires, the light turns itself back off automatically (as if it were a momentary trigger). If "Reset switch sequence when the light turns off" is also enabled, this auto-off resets the rotation too.

statefulSwitches.title: Make switches directly triggerable
statefulSwitches.description: Off (default): switches are read-only "single press" buttons you can only react to, not trigger yourself. On: switches become ordinary settable HomeKit switches, so a scene, automation, or a tap in the Home app can turn a specific switch on directly. Doing so jumps the rotation to that switch, so the next time the light turns on, it fires the switch that follows it - regardless of where the rotation was before. Either way, a fired switch turns itself back off about a second later, so it can be triggered again.

switchNames.title: Custom Switch Names (optional)
switchNames.description: Optional display names for each switch, in order (first entry = switch 1). Leave empty to auto-name them "<Light Name> Switch <n>".
